decisions.reason: As a dietary supplement line that builds on the firm's existing consumer-health and portfolio-broadening capabilities, it is close to what the firm already knows and can improve with its in-house development resources.
This skin and hair supplement is a related extension of the established offer, so the firm is likely to retain it and learn from market feedback rather than exit quickly.
Joint-health supplements fit the firm's related knowledge base and pharmacy-oriented channels, which supports continued commercialization despite only limited observed evidence after launch.
Although somewhat more novel in concept, this immune supplement still builds on the firm's existing supplement range and can be supported by its R&D, quality, and marketing capabilities.

Because this generic blood-pressure product is described as distant from the firm's established offer and already showed an early quality-related problem, management would be relatively likely to withdraw it to protect resources and reputation.

The OTC migraine triptan is also distant from the firm's established knowledge base, and with limited evidence of traction management would be inclined to redeploy resources to closer, more learnable products.
